candidates.reason: Shared base for the HTTP download-handler tests; it already carries the narrow filterwarnings markers for dependency-origin TLS deprecations (ssl.TLSVersion.TLSv1, cryptography X.509) and the pyOpenSSL/Twisted version gates that the VCS environment perturbs.
The downloader context-factory tests are the repository's dedicated warning regression tests for the pyOpenSSL/Twisted TLS implementation that the VCS workflow installs from development branches.
Twisted HTTP/1.1 download-handler coverage inherits the dependency-sensitive HTTPS/TLS cases, so it is the first place new Twisted development-branch warnings or API changes surface.
Exercises httpx2, which the workflow installs from its development branch, and reuses the same certificate/TLS assertions that emit dependency-origin deprecation warnings.
HTTP/2 handler tests depend on development-branch Twisted and the optional h2 stack, another source of warnings and version-sensitive assertions in the VCS run.
Crawler-level TLS tests already suppress the cryptography X.509 deprecation warning, so they pin the expected certificate behavior and warning noise produced with development dependencies.
Protocol-level certificate handling is warning-sensitive and depends on the Twisted/h2 development revisions installed by the VCS workflow.
Verifies Scrapy's own warning plumbing, so it detects any change that makes warning filtering too broad or alters Scrapy-origin warning messages.
The only test that reads tox configuration and asserts dependency-version contracts, matching the workflow and tox environment that the change touches.
